title: Practice Keyboard Typing and System Exploration
description: Learn keyboard layout, practice typing skills, and explore basic system tools
objective: Students will learn the keyboard layout, identify different types of keys, practice basic typing in Notepad, and explore system tools like Calculator and Paint.

steps.title: Learn the Keyboard Layout
steps.instructions:
The keyboard is the most important input device. A standard keyboard has **104 keys** divided into several groups.

**Identify these key groups on your keyboard:**

| Group | Keys | Location |
|-------|------|----------|
| Alphabet Keys | A to Z | Centre of keyboard |
| Number Keys | 0 to 9 | Top row |
| Function Keys | F1 to F12 | Very top row |
| Numeric Keypad | 0-9, +, -, *, / | Right side |
| Arrow Keys | Up, Down, Left, Right | Between main keys and numpad |
| Special Keys | Enter, Space, Backspace, Tab, Esc, Shift, Ctrl, Alt | Various locations |
| Navigation Keys | Home, End, Page Up, Page Down, Insert, Delete | Above arrow keys |
| Windows Key | Windows logo | Between Ctrl and Alt |

**Practice finding these keys quickly:**
1. Press **Caps Lock** — notice the light turn on. Type your name. It appears in UPPERCASE. Press Caps Lock again to turn it off.
2. Press **Num Lock** — the numpad on the right works for numbers only when Num Lock is ON.
3. Hold **Shift** and press a letter — it types in uppercase without Caps Lock.
4. Press **Tab** — it moves the cursor forward by one tab space.

**CCC Exam Connection:** The standard keyboard has 104 keys. Function keys are F1 to F12. F1 = Help in most programs.

steps.title: Practice Important Keyboard Shortcuts
steps.instructions:
Keyboard shortcuts save time. These shortcuts are frequently asked in the CCC exam.

**Open Notepad first:**
1. Press **Windows key** to open Start Menu
2. Type **Notepad** and press **Enter**
3. A blank Notepad window opens

**Now practice each shortcut:**

| Shortcut | What It Does | Try It Now |
|----------|-------------|------------|
| Ctrl + A | Select All text | Type some text first, then press Ctrl+A |
| Ctrl + C | Copy selected text | Select text with Ctrl+A, then press Ctrl+C |
| Ctrl + V | Paste copied text | Click at the end, press Enter, then Ctrl+V |
| Ctrl + X | Cut selected text | Select text, press Ctrl+X (text disappears) |
| Ctrl + Z | Undo last action | Press Ctrl+Z to bring back the cut text |
| Ctrl + S | Save the file | Press Ctrl+S, name it "shortcut-practice.txt" |
| Ctrl + N | Open new document | Opens a new blank Notepad |
| Ctrl + P | Print | Opens print dialog (press Cancel for now) |
| Ctrl + F | Find text | Type a word to search for |
| Alt + F4 | Close the program | DO NOT press now — it will close Notepad |

**Practice task:**
1. Type: `I am learning keyboard shortcuts at TechPath Institute`
2. Select all text (Ctrl + A)
3. Copy it (Ctrl + C)
4. Press Enter twice to go to a new line
5. Paste it (Ctrl + V)
6. Save the file (Ctrl + S) to Desktop as `shortcut-practice.txt`

**CCC Exam Connection:** Ctrl+C (Copy), Ctrl+V (Paste), Ctrl+X (Cut), Ctrl+Z (Undo) are asked in almost every CCC exam.

steps.title: Type a Paragraph in Notepad
steps.instructions:
Now let us practice typing a full paragraph. This will help you become comfortable with the keyboard.

**Open a new Notepad** (Ctrl + N) and type the following paragraph exactly as shown. Pay attention to capital letters, punctuation, and numbers:

```
Computer Fundamentals - TechPath Institute
==========================================

A computer is an electronic device that processes data into information.
Charles Babbage is known as the Father of Computer. He designed the
Analytical Engine in 1837.

The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the brain of the computer.
It has three parts:
1. ALU - Arithmetic Logic Unit (performs calculations)
2. CU - Control Unit (manages and coordinates)
3. Registers - small, fast memory inside CPU

Memory Types:
- RAM (Random Access Memory) = Volatile (data lost when power is OFF)
- ROM (Read Only Memory) = Non-volatile (data stays when power is OFF)

Important Sizes:
- 1 Byte = 8 Bits
- 1 KB = 1024 Bytes
- 1 MB = 1024 KB
- 1 GB = 1024 MB
- 1 TB = 1024 GB

ASCII Values: A=65, a=97, 0=48
```

**After typing:**
1. Save the file as `computer-notes.txt` on your Desktop (Ctrl + S)
2. Count how many minutes it took you to type this paragraph
3. Check for any spelling mistakes by reading through carefully
4. Use Ctrl + F to find the word "RAM" in your text

**CCC Exam Connection:** Notepad is a basic text editor that comes with Windows. It creates .txt files.

steps.title: Explore Calculator and Paint
steps.instructions:
Windows comes with useful built-in programs. Let us explore two of them.

**Part A — Windows Calculator:**

1. Press **Windows key**, type **Calculator**, press Enter
2. The calculator opens in **Standard** mode
3. Perform these calculations:
   - 1024 x 1024 = ? (This is 1 MB in bytes — should give 1,048,576)
   - 8 x 1024 = ? (This is 1 KB in bits — should give 8,192)
   - 256 / 8 = ? (This is how many bytes in 256 bits — should give 32)

4. Now switch to **Programmer** mode:
   - Click the menu (three lines) at the top left
   - Select **Programmer**
   - Type **13** (in DEC mode)
   - Look at the BIN row — it shows **1101** (binary of 13)
   - Look at the OCT row — it shows **15** (octal of 13)
   - Look at the HEX row — it shows **D** (hexadecimal of 13)

5. Try converting these numbers and note the binary equivalents:
   - 5 in decimal = ______ in binary
   - 10 in decimal = ______ in binary
   - 25 in decimal = ______ in binary
   - 255 in decimal = ______ in binary

**Part B — Microsoft Paint:**

1. Press **Windows key**, type **Paint**, press Enter
2. Paint is a simple drawing program
3. **Draw a simple diagram of a computer system:**
   - Draw a rectangle in the centre — label it "CPU"
   - Inside the CPU rectangle, write "ALU", "CU", "Registers"
   - Draw input devices on the left (keyboard shape, mouse shape)
   - Draw output devices on the right (monitor shape, printer shape)
   - Draw arrows showing: Input → CPU → Output
   - Draw a memory box connected to CPU — label it "RAM + ROM"

4. Save your drawing as `computer-diagram.png` on the Desktop

**CCC Exam Connection:** Calculator and Paint are application software that comes pre-installed with Windows.

steps.title: Complete the Review Quiz
steps.instructions:
Let us test what you learned in this lab. Answer these questions on paper or in a new Notepad file.

**Part A — True or False:**

1. A keyboard is an output device. (True / False)
2. RAM is volatile memory. (True / False)
3. ROM stores the BIOS. (True / False)
4. 1 KB = 1000 Bytes. (True / False)
5. Ctrl + V is the shortcut for Copy. (True / False)
6. The CPU has two parts: ALU and CU. (True / False)
7. Charles Babbage invented the mouse. (True / False)
8. A printer produces hard copy output. (True / False)

**Part B — Fill in the blanks:**

1. The shortcut to Select All is Ctrl + ___.
2. The shortcut to Undo is Ctrl + ___.
3. A standard keyboard has ___ keys.
4. 1 Byte = ___ Bits.
5. The ASCII value of 'A' is ___.

**Part C — Matching:**

Match the shortcut to its function:

| Shortcut | Function |
|----------|----------|
| 1. Ctrl + C | a. Paste |
| 2. Ctrl + X | b. Save |
| 3. Ctrl + V | c. Copy |
| 4. Ctrl + S | d. Close program |
| 5. Alt + F4 | e. Cut |

**Answers:** 1-c, 2-e, 3-a, 4-b, 5-d

**Submit your completed work (Notepad files, Paint diagram, and quiz answers) to your trainer.**
